summary: pylever exfiltrates Discord tokens and account metadata to a hardcoded webhook
details: pylever scans the installer's workspace files, Chromium/Edge/Firefox/Brave Local Storage, leveldb and Cache directories, and the Discord Desktop application data directory, regex-matching Discord user and bot tokens ([MN][A-Za-z0-9_-]{71}). Each candidate token is validated against discord.com/api/v10/users/@me, and validated tokens are then POSTed together with the associated username, discriminator, user id, email, verified flag and bot flag to a hardcoded Discord webhook at discord.com/api/webhooks/1547416857537945601/... controlled by the package author. setup.py and pyproject.toml carry placeholder author metadata ("Your Name", "your.email@example.com", github.com/yourusername/pylever) while the shipped code implements this credential-harvesting behavior, and the package's stated purpose ("find and save Discord bot tokens via webhook") aligns with the harmful behavior itself.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
